finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::user sql is string-interpolated into the executed statement and gated only by a keyword blacklist, permitting server file reads / ssrf / non-blacklisted ddl-free abuse
evidence: The code matches the claim: `datasource.service.ts:148` builds `SELECT * FROM (${dto.query}) AS _q LIMIT ...` by raw string interpolation, and the only gate is `validateSelectQuery` (sql-validator.ts), which just checks the first token is SELECT/WITH, rejects a fixed `\b`-delimited keyword list (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/ALTER/CREATE/TRUNCATE/GRANT/REVOKE/EXEC/EXECUTE), and rejects multiple statements. None of those checks block `SELECT pg_read_file(...)`, `SELECT pg_ls_dir('/')`, `SELECT lo_import(...)`, `dblink(...)`, or `pg_terminate_backend(...)`, all of which are single SELECT statements that survive the subquery wrapping; the controller only asserts workspace membership (datasource.controller.ts POST /datasources/:id/query), so any member can run them against an admin-configured connection. Caveats that bound impact: the dangerous functions require superuser/`pg_read_server_files` privileges or the dblink extension on the target DB, and this is pre-existing behavior the diff merely extends (docs/design/sheets/datasource.md already lists it as a known risk with "consider a read-only role"). The claim is nonetheless accurate about the code as written.
